items.title: Percy Stovall Interview, 1977-12-27
items.q: Him and Hewlett Smith was tight because they used to be room buddies, you know.

ctx.x: Sometimes they'll take it off the top and they don't know how much they're actually paying. Right, right, right. That's what happened. How do you treat people in his band? Somebody told me he had sort of an ego problem. Did you find that?

I don't think so. I don't think he did. I mean, you know, he got along with the members of the band, alright, because they're always drinking. He was drinking and the member of the band was drinking, you know. So I don't think he, you might have, you see, he was a musician, he didn't know music. He only played by, yeah, you know, and he used a thing on his guitar called a choker. And if they took that choker he couldn't go on. Well sometimes they'd do it just to kick something, hide it, you know, almost time for…
Used to call him Poor Devil?

items.title: Percy Stovall Interview, 1977-12-27
items.q: Hewlett used to call him Poor Devil. Come on, answer the door for me. ... Hewlett called him Poor Devil.

Yeah, Poor Devil. And he used to call Hewlett Death. Hewlett was so puny looking, you know, and he never would get up, when he'd go to bed at night from the, yeah, he never'd get the time to get up. He'd never get the time to go to the gig next year, he wouldn't get the heat or nothing, just to rent a bed all day. So Slim used to call him Death, and Hewlett called him Poor Devil.
